I have resolved the issue where deferred fields were incorrectly overwritten when following prefetches back to the parent object.

### Cause
When evaluating nested `prefetch_related` lookups back to a parent object (such as `Prefetch('profile', queryset=Profile.objects.prefetch_related(Prefetch('user', queryset=User.objects.only('kind'))))`), the inner prefetch populates the relation cache on `profile` with the inner `User` instance (which has fields specified in its own `only(...)` queryset). However, the prefetch logic in `ForwardManyToOneDescriptor`, `ReverseOneToOneDescriptor`, and `ReverseManyToOneDescriptor` was unconditionally overwriting the cached relation on each prefetched object with the outer parent instance (which had a different set of deferred fields).

### Fix
Updated `ForwardManyToOneDescriptor.get_prefetch_queryset`, `ReverseOneToOneDescriptor.get_prefetch_queryset`, and `ReverseManyToOneDescriptor.get_prefetch_queryset` in [`django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py`](file:///testbed/django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py) to check `is_cached(...)` before assigning the back-reference on prefetched objects, preventing existing cached instances from being overwritten.
